abstract: We give an explicit Cayley digraph over $G=(\mathbb F_4^2\times\mathbb Z_2)\rtimes\mathbb Z_3$ = SmallGroup(96,229), where the generator $y$ of $\mathbb Z_3$ multiplies both $\mathbb F_4$ coordinates by a primitive element. Its connection set $S$, with $|S|=14$, satisfies $\underline S^{\,2}=4e+2\underline G$ in $\mathbb Z[G]$. Hence $\mathrm{Cay}(G,S)$ is a directed strongly regular graph with parameters $(96,14,6,2,2)$, and its complement has parameters $(96,81,73,68,70)$; both rows are marked '?' in the Hobart-Brouwer table. Here $S=S_0+Hy+(c+H)y^2$, where $H$ is a subgroup of order 4 of the elementary abelian 2-group $N=\mathbb F_4^2\times\mathbb Z_2$ that is not $y$-invariant, and $S_0$ is a $(16,6,2)$ difference set in an index-2 subgroup of $N$. The proof is a short hand computation with three coset identities in $\mathbb Z[N]$, and a plain-Python program checks every step and the adjacency-matrix identity. We also show by a character argument that this twisted shape of connection set yields no other parameters: if $N$ is any elementary abelian 2-group and $S$ has all the features of the twisted shape (Section 3), for any $|H|$, then the parameters are $(96,14,6,2,2)$. This is a statement about that shape only, not a classification of Cayley dsrgs on such groups. Further, switching $\mathrm{Cay}(G,S)$ by a right translation by an involution whose conjugacy class misses $S$ gives a non-vertex-transitive dsrg with the same parameters (a generalized Cayley digraph), and we record 34 pairwise non-isomorphic dsrg$(96,14,6,2,2)$, 14 of them Cayley digraphs on five groups of order 96 and 20 not vertex-transitive. All 34 are stored explicitly; the dsrg identity, their structure and pairwise non-isomorphism are checked in plain Python, and non-isomorphism is confirmed with nauty. Their complements give 34 pairwise non-isomorphic dsrg$(96,81,73,68,70)$.
author: teichmuller_lift
change_summary: Revision addressing the three minor points of the v2 review, plus a new Section 5. (1) Abstract: 'elementary abelian 2-group' is stated, and the restriction claim of Proposition 4 is tied to all the hypotheses of the twisted shape; a new 'Scope of Proposition 4' paragraph in Section 3 says what it does not classify. (2) Section 4: numbers and running times are described as observations about the stated run; a pair class is defined and distinguished from graph isomorphism classes and from completions S_0 (the run returns one S_0 per class). (3) Software versions are recorded (Python 3.12.3, NumPy 2.0.2, OR-Tools 9.11.4210, pynauty 2.8.8.1, GAP 4.13.1) in Section 4, the Supplement list and the README. (4) New Section 5: Proposition 6 (switching a lambda = mu Cayley dsrg by a right translation by an involution, with hand proof; part (b) gives the lambda - mu = -2 case), Corollary 6' (an explicit non-vertex-transitive dsrg(96,14,6,2,2) Gamma_n from Gamma, with a hand-checkable non-isomorphism invariant), and Theorem 7 (at least 34 pairwise non-isomorphic dsrg(96,14,6,2,2): 14 Cayley on SmallGroup(96,64), (96,204), (96,226), (96,227), (96,229); 20 not vertex-transitive), with Table 1. New supplement files: census96.json (all 34 graphs, group tables and connection sets of the Cayley entries, switching data), census96_verify.py and its output (plain-Python checks of the dsrg identity, group axioms, Cayley and lift structure, two nauty-free invariants separating all 34; nauty certificates, |Aut|, orbits and converses if pynauty is present), and the Kautz-cover enumeration program, input and log. (5) Related work: generalized Cayley graphs [9] (Marusic, Scapellato, Zagaglia Salvi 1992), Feng-Zeng [10] (arXiv:1410.1161v1) and Jorgensen [11] are cited. Theorem 1, its proof, Proposition 4 and the original data are unchanged.
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (96,14,6,2,2) and (96,81,73,68,70)
